I have been growing stevia here in Quzhou for about eight years now. Before that I grew wheat and maize, but the stevia buyer comes right to the village and the price is steady, so I switched. I plant the chengguang variety — it is an improved kind, not the old wild type. The seedlings I buy from the input dealer in town. My neighbor Lao Wang plants the same kind. Last year his yield was good, around 550 kilos per mu, so I will stick with it.

My piece of land is only 1.1 mu, very small. Every yuan I spend on inputs is real money, but a bad harvest is worse than wasting a little fertilizer. Last year I put down one bag of compound fertilizer, 15-15-15, about 50 kilos, and then I topdressed with half a bag of urea later when the plants were growing fast. This year I will do the same, maybe a bit more compound because the dealer said stevia needs plenty of fertilizer to make big leaves. I also irrigate five times from my well — once right after planting in early April, then two times in June when it gets hot, once in July, and one more before harvest in August. The pump uses electricity, so five times is enough. I cannot afford to water like the big farms do.

For pests, I spray insecticide three times, mainly for aphids and leaf-eating worms. I also spray herbicide once after planting to keep the weeds down, and if the weather is rainy I might spray fungicide once. That makes five times total. I rotary till the soil before planting — everyone around here does rotary tillage, it breaks up the soil fine for the small seedlings. I do the work myself and my wife helps. We do not hire labor for 1.1 mu, that would waste money.

I expect to get about 550 kilos per mu this year, same as last year if the weather cooperates. I am not changing much. Last year worked, so why take risks?
